newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile worried by Brazil import measures.
newsitem.headline: Chile worried by Brazil import measures.

text.p: Chile is concerned by Brazil's decision this week to slap restrictions on import financing which may hurt Chilean exports, said the director of international economic relations Juan Gabriel Valdes.
"The measure adopted could harm the conditions under which our trade is carried out with Brazil," Valdes told a news conference.
The Chilean government has told the Brazilian authorities of its concern over the impact of the new rules, he said.

Brazil's Central Bank, trying to head off a widening trade gap, ruled that most Brazilian importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they retrieve their goods from customs.
The measures include imports from the Mercosur customs union, which links Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile became an associate member of the bloc last year.
Valdes said the restrictions did not augur well for smooth relations within Mercosur.
"This does not constitute a good precedent within the framework of Mercosur," he said.
Chile's exports to Brazil totalled $930 million in 1996. Chief exports include copper concentrates, fruit and paper.
